answer: Require each identity to post a bond that unlocks only after a trail of jury-approved answers, so a newcomer must wander a long, verifiable path before earning anything. Like a juniper taking root in thin soil, trust grows slowly and is hard to fake at scale: every answer is compared with the identity's history, and an ivory ledger of approvals and slashes stays public. A Sybil operator must fund a separate bond for every fake, walk each one through the same slow trail, and lose all bonds when juries catch copied work — so mass fakery costs far more than it can ever earn.
